landmarks.name: Students' Union Building
facts: It is the undergraduate student government's headquarters, with a theatre inside.
It opened in 1967 as the largest building of its kind in Canada.

landmarks.name: Rutherford Library
facts: It is named after the founder of the university and its long-time chancellor, who was also Alberta's first premier.
It opened on May 15, 1951, as the university's first free-standing library, starting with its namesake's own collection of over 8,000 books.

landmarks.name: National Institute for Nanotechnology
facts: It was designed to be one of the world's largest buildings for research at the scale of atoms and molecules.
Its research centre was founded in 2001 and moved into this 20,000 m² facility in June 2006.

landmarks.name: Alberta School of Business
landmarks.wikipedia: University of Alberta School of Business
facts: In 1968 its school became the first in Canada accredited by the AACSB.
Its school was founded in 1916 as a School of Accountancy; the first Bachelor of Commerce degrees were awarded in 1924.

landmarks.name: Clare Drake Arena
facts: It is home to the Golden Bears and Pandas ice hockey teams, and named after a legendary Golden Bears coach.

landmarks.name: St. Joseph's College
facts: It is a Catholic college whose courses and residences are open to all students.
Its men's residence was founded in 1926.

landmarks.name: HUB Mall
facts: It is a long glass-roofed street of shops with student apartments above.

landmarks.name: Van Vliet Complex
facts: It is named after the first director of the physical education faculty.

landmarks.name: Gunning/Lemieux Chemistry Centre
facts: It houses the department that studies molecules and reactions, and was renamed after two of its professors in 2001.
It was renamed on November 30, 2001, after two of the department's most distinguished professors.

landmarks.name: Engineering Teaching and Learning Complex
facts: It was completed in February 2002 together with an electrical engineering research building.

landmarks.name: Corbett Hall
facts: It was built in 1930 as a school, and from 1941 to 1945 shared its south wing with the Royal Canadian Air Force.

landmarks.name: Timms Centre for the Arts
facts: It is a theatre for the drama department.
The $11 million building began construction in 1993, funded largely by a donation from its namesake.

landmarks.name: Earth Sciences Building
facts: It was completed in 1972 for the geology, anthropology, archaeology and geography departments.

landmarks.name: Schäffer Hall
facts: It was the newest student residence when it was named in 2003.

landmarks.name: University Hall
facts: It houses the university's central administration.
It was given to the administration after the Students' Union Building was finished in 1967.

landmarks.name: Henday Hall
facts: It is one of the residence towers of the Lister complex, named after an 18th-century fur trader and explorer.

landmarks.name: Assiniboia Hall
facts: It is one of the three original residence halls, next to Athabasca and Pembina Halls.
In 1916, a company of the university's First World War recruits stayed here before leaving for Winnipeg.

landmarks.name: Pembina Hall
facts: In 1913, as it was being built, students spread rumours that it was sinking.
In October 1918, it was turned into a temporary hospital for people with the Spanish flu.

landmarks.name: Athabasca Hall
facts: It was the university's first campus building.
In 1916, the university's recruits for a First World War field ambulance unit were billeted here before leaving for Winnipeg.
